summary:
--- PART 1/4 ---
ORIGIN: "Wait probes begin with ten externally supplied CC rounds, then runs 24 further rounds. one_D_TFT uses one initial defections followed by copying your last action. Hmm controlled probe begins with ten CC rounds? Need parse: "Each controlled probe begins with ten externally supplied CC rounds, then runs 24 further rounds. These histories need not be naturally reachable. one_D_TFT and four_D_TFT use one or four initial defections followed by copying your last action; four_D_ALLC uses four defections followed by unconditional cooperation; sustained_D always defects; periodic_D defects on the first two positions of each five-round cycle." So history supplied first 10 rounds are CC. Then probe acts according to rule for 24 rounds, probably against our strategy." "Maybe "four_D_TFT use four initial defections" refers to the probe's entire match? Actually "one_D_TFT and four_D_TFT use one or four initial defections followed by copying your last action" might mean the probe's strategy is TFT with initial one/four defections at the start of the match, not after ten CC. But the controlled probe begins with ten externally supplied CC rounds. So those ten CC are not generated by probe's strategy; they are fed as history to our strategy. Then we play 24 rounds against the probe. The probe's behavior during those 24 rounds is determined by its rule and the history? The probe sees the history including ten CC? For one_D_TFT, "one initial defection followed by copying your last action" might mean at the start of the 24-round segment, it defects once then TFT. So round 11 opponent D, round 12 copies our round 11 action, etc. For four_D_TFT, rounds 11-14 opponent D, round 15 copies our round 14, etc. My analysis matches that. But measured own_cooperation_first4=0.75 for four_D_TFT, meaning our first 4 rounds of 24: C,D,C,D? That's 0.5. Unless parent's behavior differs due to n counting includes 10 CC."

CONTRADICTION: "Why measured four_D_TFT says not_recovered=1, mutual_cooperation_last5=0? Maybe my analysis off due to probe definition" "But measured parent: own_cooperation_after4=0.5, own_cooperation_first4=0.75, own_cooperation_last5=0.6, mutual_cooperation_last5=0.0, not_recovered=1, recovery_time_capped=20, score=2.125. Wait maybe "own_cooperation_after4" means our cooperation rate in first 4 rounds after the probe's initial defections? Let's parse metrics: own_cooperation_first4=0.75: our cooperation rate in first 4 rounds of the 24? The probes begin with ten CC, then 24 further rounds. For four_D_TFT, probe defects for first four of the 24? Then copies. Our cooperation in first 4 = 0.75 means we cooperated 3 of first 4? But my analysis said round 11 C, 12 D, 13 C, 14 D -> 0.5. So mismatch."

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Let's recalc parent at n=10, history first 10 are CC. n=10, op_last C. Parent goes to else. n>=2: recent_my = last 3 my actions: all C. recent_op all C. all(m=='D') false. n>90 false. returns C. So round 11: we C. Opponent (probe) defects? If four_D_TFT has four initial defections, round 11 opponent D. Good." "Thus first 4 rounds (11-14): C,C,D,C -> cooperation rate 0.75. Yes! I earlier had round 11 C, 12 D, but parent actually forgives at n=11 because opp_def=1 <= max(1,1). So round 12 C. Then round 13 D. Round 14 C. So first4=0.75. Good."

STRATEGY: Parent is mostly TFT with forgiveness and exploit. Simulated controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) against parent. Changed/considered: improve recovery from four_D_TFT by forgiving after defection streaks, exploit always cooperators, defect sooner against always defectors, and adjust endgame.

--- PART 2/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent got 2.875 against one_D_TFT. So we are slightly worse." / "Parent got 2.875. Let's see why parent did better." / "That matches measured parent one_D_TFT score 2.875."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates initially, forgives first defections, retaliates after repeated defections, and defects in the endgame. The trace simulates modified TFT/probing variants against controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, sustained_D, etc.) and changes forgiveness thresholds, probe timing, and defection-streak rules to improve recovery and exploitation.

--- PART 3/4 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent's measured four_D_TFT score was 2.1250. Over 24 rounds, that's 51." and "So a simple fix: in the op_last == 'D' branch, if opp_def_streak >= 4 (or >=3?), return C."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-with-forgiveness strategy that cooperates after long CC, forgives limited defections, and defects in endgame. The trace simulates modified versions against four_D_TFT, one_D_TFT, periodic_D, sustained_D, and always-C probes. Changes considered: break opponent defection streaks >=3 by cooperating, add an always-C probe at n=30, adjust forgiveness thresholds, and add last-round defection.

ORIGIN: NONE

RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "The parent's high fitness suggests its behavior against the actual population is good. We should not overfit to the probes at the expense of real performance."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like strategy with forgiveness/retaliation rules; simulated controlled probes (one_D_TFT, four_D_TFT, four_D_ALLC, sustained_D, periodic_D) and tournament scenarios; changed forgiveness to forgive only when opp_def_streak is 3–5 and opp_c > n*0.3, added an n=30 probe, and adjusted endgame n=98/n=99 behavior.
